hook: Read a short story about a window opened every night at nine, and uncover what the ritual really meant.
intro: The capstone reading: a first-person story (the narrator is the grandchild) about a grandmother who opened the kitchen window every evening at nine for a quarter of an hour, in every season, long after anyone came. Her stated reason – „Damit die Luft sich nicht an die Stille gewöhnt“ – is given halb im Scherz. The middle of the story supplies the background (a once-full house, the grandfather who tapped on the pane shortly after nine, children and neighbours gone). After the funeral the narrator’s mother catches herself at the window at nine, and only then („Erst in diesem Augenblick begriff sie …“) understands what the ritual was – the text states it with „nicht …, sondern …“ and explicitly excludes the obvious answer. A generalising last sentence turns one gesture into a statement about gestures. The eight questions move from action to stated reason, background, the moment of realisation, its content and the final sentence – the full arc of reading a literary text closely.
tips[0].title: Ritual + stated reason + halb im Scherz
tips[0].text: A ritual described in detail, a reason that sounds like a joke, and a narrator who tells you it was only half a joke: the other half is serious, and the story will uncover it. Note the details of the ritual precisely – the questions check them.
tips[0].check.why: Half a joke means the other half is serious; the story will reveal the real reason later.
tips[0].visual.moves[0].label: Ritual
tips[0].visual.moves[1].label: Stated reason
tips[0].visual.moves[2].label: Realisation
tips[1].title: Erst … begriff: the realisation, and what it excludes
tips[1].text: „Erst in diesem Augenblick begriff sie …“ marks the turning point. The content of the realisation follows in a „nicht …, sondern …“ chain – and here the text also says what it is NOT about, including the answer most readers would guess.
tips[1].trap: The grandfather tapping on the pane at nine is the most tempting explanation – and the text rules it out in so many words (auch nicht auf den Großvater).
tips[1].check.why: Erst … begriff marks the realisation, and its content stands in the sondern-half; sie is explicitly ruled out.
tips[2].title: The last sentence generalises
tips[2].text: From one window to all gestures. To answer „Wie ist der Schlusssatz zu verstehen?“ paraphrase it in plain terms and check it against the story: the grandmother never named her reason, and the mother continues the ritual in silence.
tips[2].check.why: The sentence generalises: explaining a silence destroys what it says, so understanding means leaving it unexplained.
remember[0]: Ritual → stated reason (halb im Scherz) → background → Erst … begriff → generalising last sentence.
remember[1]: In the realisation, read every „nicht“: the text excludes the air AND the grandfather.
remember[2]: The last sentence explains the joke in hindsight: naming the reason would have destroyed the gesture.
exam: Close reading of a short literary text is part of the C2 exam — and what turns reading a story into understanding it.
tips[0].check.q: „Er sagte, er gehe nur wegen des Hundes spazieren, halb im Scherz.“ What does halb im Scherz signal?
tips[0].check.options[0]: The reason is partly true, and there is a serious reason too.
tips[0].check.options[2]: He did not have a dog.
tips[0].check.answer: The reason is partly true, and there is a serious reason too.
tips[1].check.q: „Erst als der Zug abfuhr, begriff er, dass er nicht auf sie gewartet hatte, sondern auf einen Grund zu bleiben.“ What had he been waiting for?
tips[2].check.q: Final sentence: „Wer jedes Schweigen erklärt, hat nichts verstanden.“ Which paraphrase fits?
tips[2].check.options[0]: Some silences keep their meaning only if nobody explains them.
tips[2].check.options[1]: People should explain their silences more.
tips[2].check.options[2]: Silence is always a sign of misunderstanding.
tips[2].check.answer: Some silences keep their meaning only if nobody explains them.
